concept.name: Low price
concept.definition: The low price is the lowest price at which any trade executed during a given period. It marks the lower extreme of the period's traded range and forms the bottom of an OHLC bar or candlestick wick.
concept.intuition: The low is the least anyone received (or paid) for the asset during the period — the trough of the price excursion.
concept.mechanics: Computed as the minimum of all executed trade prices within the aggregation interval; rendered as the bottom of the vertical line (OHLC bar) or lower shadow (candlestick).
concept.formula: L = min(p_i) over all trades i in the period.
concept.failure_modes: Erroneous prints or illiquid spikes can create false lows, which matters for stop-loss placement and range computations. The low carries no information about the volume traded at that extreme.
concept.misconceptions: The low is not automatically a support level — it is merely the minimum executed price of the period.
concept.example: If a stock's trades during the day range from $48.25 to $50.00, the daily low is $48.25 even if price immediately bounced from that print.
